nodes.title: For any past date, get the stocks that were investable on that date and their total returns, using only what was known then.
Know where the data might be wrong: every disagreement with an independent source is flagged, then explained or accepted.
See the data and its quality issues visually, without writing code.
Total returns as of a date
For a given date, the system returns every stock that was an S&P 500 member during that date, by the date each index change took effect.

criteria: Given an index addition announced on day A and effective on day E > A, when the universe is requested for any day from A to E − 1, then the stock is not in it; when requested for day E, then it is.
Given an index removal effective on day R, when the universe is requested for day R − 1, then the stock is in it; for day R, then it is not.

nodes.title: The universe for a date includes members that later left the index or stopped trading.

criteria: Given 2008-06-02, when the universe is requested, then Lehman Brothers, Bear Stearns, Countrywide, Merrill Lynch, Wachovia and Anheuser-Busch are all in it.

nodes.title: Each stock has a permanent identifier for the company, which is unchanged across ticker changes.

criteria: Given a company that changed ticker, when its membership is requested for dates before and after the change, then both carry the same identifier.

nodes.title: Each returned member carries the ticker it traded under on the requested date.

criteria: Given 2005-06-01, when the universe is requested, then the entry for Anheuser-Busch shows ticker BUD and the company is Anheuser-Busch, not today's holder of that ticker.

nodes.title: The system returns the number of members for every trading day in a date range.

criteria: Given 1998-01-02 to the latest loaded day, when universe sizes are requested, then every trading day has a count, and each count equals the length of that day's universe list.

nodes.title: For every stock that was investable on any date since 1998, the system returns its daily total-return series between two given dates.

criteria: Given any date D since 1998-01-02 and the universe for D, when total returns from D to D + 20 trading days are requested, then a series is returned for every member, including members that stopped trading in that window.

nodes.title: A daily total return combines the price change and any cash dividend going ex on that day.

criteria: Given a stock with a $0.50 dividend going ex on day T, a close of $50.00 on T − 1 and a close of $49.75 on T, when returns are requested, then the return for T is (49.75 + 0.50) / 50.00 − 1 = +0.50%.

nodes.title: Daily total returns are unaffected by stock splits.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split effective on day T with closes of $100.00 on T − 1 and $50.50 on T, when returns are requested, then the return for T is +1.00%.

nodes.title: Results requested as of date D use no information published after D.

criteria: Given a split or dividend that goes ex after D, when returns or prices are requested as of D, then the values up to D are identical to those produced before that event was loaded.

nodes.title: Price levels are available unadjusted, or adjusted only for splits and dividends that went ex on or before the as-of date.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split on day S > D, when adjusted prices are requested as of D, then they equal the unadjusted prices for every day up to D.

nodes.title: A stock's return series runs through its last trading day, including the return on that last day.

criteria: Given Lehman Brothers, when returns through 2008-09-30 are requested, then the return for 2008-09-15 is present and below −90%.
Given a company acquired for cash, when returns are requested, then the return on its last trading day is present and the series ends that day.

nodes.title: Every returned series states whether each day is a trading day with a price, or a gap.

criteria: Given a trading halt with no close on day T, when returns are requested, then day T is marked as a gap and has no invented return.

nodes.title: A refresh downloads data from the primary source.

criteria: Given an empty store, when a refresh is started, then afterwards prices, corporate actions, company identities and index membership are stored for every S&P 500 member from 1998-01-02 to the last completed trading day.

nodes.title: A refresh fetches only data newer than what is already stored.

criteria: Given data stored through day T, when a refresh is started on day T + 1 after the close, then only day T + 1 and any corrections the source issued since the last refresh are downloaded.

nodes.title: A refresh cleans the data before it is stored.

criteria: Given a downloaded row with a duplicate (stock, date), when the refresh runs, then one row is stored and the duplicate is reported in the run summary.

nodes.title: A refresh ends with a validation run (CHECK-01), and its results go to the run summary.

criteria: Given a completed refresh, when its summary is viewed, then it lists the number of rows added, rows changed, and new findings.

nodes.title: A refresh that fails leaves the stored data as it was before the refresh started.

criteria: Given a refresh interrupted after half its downloads, when the universe or returns are requested, then the results are identical to those before the refresh.

nodes.title: A refresh started while another is running is refused.

criteria: Given a refresh in progress, when a second is started, then it is refused with a message naming the running one.

nodes.title: Each run of a refresh or validation is started on demand, from the command line or from the app.

criteria: Given the app open, when the researcher starts a refresh there, then it runs exactly as one started from the command line.

nodes.title: A validation run checks 100 members that the independent source still carries, sampled across 1998 to today.

criteria: Given a validation run, when it finishes, then it has compared exactly 100 stocks (or all available, if fewer), and every calendar year from 1998 to today has at least 2 stocks that were members in that year.

nodes.title: For each sampled stock, the run also checks every split and special dividend that stock had.

criteria: Given a sampled stock with 3 splits and 1 special dividend since 1998, when the run finishes, then all 4 events have been compared.

nodes.title: A full validation run, on demand, checks every member the independent source carries.

criteria: Given a full validation run, when it finishes, then every member the independent source carries has been compared.

nodes.title: Splits agree only when the date and the ratio match exactly.

criteria: Given a 3-for-2 split on one source and a 2-for-1 split on the same date on the other, when compared, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Dividends agree only when the ex-date matches and the amount is within $0.001.

criteria: Given amounts of $0.2500 and $0.2509 on the same ex-date, when compared, then they agree; given $0.2500 and $0.2515, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Daily total returns agree when they are within 5 basis points (0.05 percentage points) of each other.

criteria: Given returns of +1.20% and +1.24% for the same stock and day, when compared, then they agree; given +1.20% and +1.26%, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Unadjusted closes agree when they are within 0.5% of each other.

criteria: Given closes of $40.00 and $40.18, when compared, then they agree; given $40.00 and $40.25, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: A stock the independent source doesn't carry is checked for missing trading days before its last trading day.

criteria: Given a delisted stock with no price on a day when the exchange was open and the stock was not halted, when checked, then a finding is raised for that day.

nodes.title: A stock acquired for a known cash price is checked for a last close consistent with the deal.

criteria: Given a cash acquisition at $70.00 a share and a last close of $69.95, when checked, then it passes; given a last close more than 2% from the deal price, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: A stock's index membership is checked to end no later than its last trading day.

criteria: Given a stock whose membership ends after its last trading day, when checked, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Findings from internal checks are listed and resolved in the same way as disagreements with the independent source.

criteria: Given a CHECK-08 finding and a CHECK-06 finding, when findings are listed, then both appear in one list with the same fields and the same resolve actions.

nodes.title: Each finding records the stock, the date(s), the check that raised it, both values, and the difference.

criteria: Given any finding, when viewed, then all five are shown.

nodes.title: The researcher resolves a finding by marking it explained, with a written reason, or accepted.

criteria: Given an open finding, when marked explained with no reason, then it is refused; with a reason, then its status becomes explained and the reason and date are kept.

nodes.title: A resolved finding stays resolved in later runs while both values are unchanged.

criteria: Given an explained finding, when the next run finds the same difference, then no new finding is raised; when either value has changed, then the finding is reopened.

nodes.title: The 10 named former members are present with both end dates matching the reference table in DATA-04.

criteria: Given each of the 10 names, when checked, then its index exit date and its last trading day on a major exchange each equal the table's value, or a finding is raised for each one that differs.

nodes.title: The exploratory analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on the full stored history. It covers summary statistics and tails of daily total returns by year, missing days per stock, universe size over time, and the number of corporate actions per year.

criteria: Given a completed refresh, when the analysis runs, then its report has a section for each of the four, covering every year from 1998 to today.

nodes.title: Each anomaly the analysis identifies becomes a finding.

criteria: Given a stock with a daily return above +100% and no corporate action on that day, when the analysis runs, then a finding is raised for that stock and day.

nodes.title: The analysis report can be opened in the app.

criteria: Given a completed analysis, when the researcher opens it in the app, then the report's tables and charts are shown.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock, the app shows its unadjusted and adjusted price history.

criteria: Given Eastman Kodak, when chosen, then both price series are shown for 1998 to its last trading day.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock, the app shows a timeline of its corporate actions, ticker changes and index entry and exit.

criteria: Given Wachovia, when chosen, then its index exit and last trading day appear on the timeline.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock that was compared, the app shows its daily differences from the independent source over time, with the agreement thresholds marked.

criteria: Given a sampled stock, when chosen, then each day beyond a CHECK-06 or CHECK-07 threshold is highlighted.

nodes.title: The app shows S&P 500 member count per trading day from 1998 to the latest loaded day.

criteria: Given the chart, when the researcher points at a day, then that day's count and date are shown.

nodes.title: The app lists findings, filterable by status, check and stock.

criteria: Given 50 findings of which 10 are open, when filtered to open, then exactly 10 are shown.

nodes.title: The researcher can resolve a finding from the app.

criteria: Given an open finding, when marked explained with a reason in the app, then its status changes as in CHECK-13.

nodes.title: For a chosen date, the app shows that date's universe.

criteria: Given 2008-06-02, when chosen, then the list shows every member with its ticker on that date.

nodes.title: The app shows data views, quality tools and the reports that commands write; it has no screening or interactive research views.

criteria: Given the app, when every page is opened, then none ranks or filters stocks by return or signal.

nodes.title: The app shows a running refresh's or validation's current step and percentage complete, updated as the run advances.

criteria: Given a running refresh, when the app is open, then the shown step and percentage change within 2 seconds of the run advancing, without reloading the page.

nodes.title: Errors and warnings appear in the app as they happen during a run.

criteria: Given a stock the independent source rejects, when it happens, then a warning naming the stock appears within 2 seconds.

nodes.title: A run started from the command line also shows its progress in the app.

criteria: Given a refresh started from the command line, when the app is opened, then the run is shown with its current progress.

nodes.title: Finished runs are listed with start time, end time, outcome and summary.

criteria: Given 3 finished runs, when the run list is opened, then all 3 are shown, newest first.

nodes.title: The structure analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on every rebalance date's window: the eligible members of PORT-03 over the 252 trading days ending that day. It passes when the report has, for every window, the eigenvalue spectrum, the market factor's share of variance, and the raw and residual mean absolute correlation.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the structure part of its report is read, then each of the three is present for every rebalance date.

nodes.title: For each window, the eigenvalues of the members' correlation matrix are compared with the random-matrix (Marchenko–Pastur) noise edge for that window's number of days and stocks, and the number of eigenvalues above the edge is reported.

criteria: Given a synthetic window of 252 days and 400 stocks with independent returns, when analysed, then at most 1 eigenvalue is above the edge.
Given a synthetic window of 252 days and 400 stocks driven by one common factor that explains 40% of each stock's variance, when analysed, then exactly 1 eigenvalue is above the edge.

nodes.title: For each window, the market factor's share of variance is the largest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix divided by the number of stocks, reported as a series over time.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when analysed, then the share is 0.40 ± 0.03.

nodes.title: For each window, the principal components above the noise edge (at least 1) are removed from every stock's returns, and the mean absolute pairwise correlation of what remains is reported next to the raw value, with the number of components removed.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when analysed, then 1 component is removed, the raw mean absolute correlation is ≥ 0.35, and the residual one is ≤ 0.08.

nodes.title: Each window's results use only the returns inside that window.

criteria: Given a return changed on a day after rebalance date R, when the study is run again, then every structure result for R and earlier windows is identical.

nodes.title: One command runs the whole study and writes one report with three parts: structure, league table and significance.

criteria: Given stored data from 1998-01-02, when the command is run, then one report is written that has all three parts.

nodes.title: Rebalance dates are the last trading day of each month, from the first month-end on which 252 trading days have passed since 1998-01-02 to the last month-end whose following month is complete.

criteria: Given data from 1998-01-02 to 2026-09-30, when the study runs, then every rebalance date is a month's last trading day, the first is the first month-end with 252 trading days behind it, and the last is 2026-08-31.

nodes.title: At each rebalance date, the portfolios hold that day's members (UNIV-01) that have 252 trading days of returns ending that day; members with fewer are left out that month, and the number left out is reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given a stock added to the index with 100 trading days of history on rebalance date R, when the study runs, then the stock is in no portfolio formed on R, and R's left-out count includes it.

nodes.title: Every estimate and every weight formed on rebalance date R uses no return from after R.

criteria: Given a return changed on a day after R, when the study is run again, then every estimate and weight formed on R or earlier is identical.

nodes.title: The sample estimate is the sample covariance of the window's daily returns.

criteria: Given a synthetic window, when estimated, then it equals the sample covariance of those returns.

nodes.title: The shrinkage estimate pulls the sample covariance toward a constant-correlation target (each stock's own sample variance, and one correlation shared by every pair equal to the window's average sample correlation), by an intensity estimated from the window and reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given any window, when estimated, then the result equals (1 − δ) × sample + δ × target with 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1, and δ is reported.

nodes.title: The denoised estimate replaces the correlation matrix's eigenvalues below the noise edge of STRUC-02 with their average, keeps those above it, and rescales to each stock's sample variance.

criteria: Given any window, when estimated, then the eigenvalues above the edge are unchanged, those below it are all equal, the matrix's trace is unchanged, and its diagonal equals the sample variances.

nodes.title: The factor-model estimate is built from the principal components above the noise edge (at least 1) plus each stock's own residual variance, and the number of components is reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when estimated, then 1 component is used and the diagonal equals the sample variances.

nodes.title: Every portfolio is long-only and fully invested: no weight is negative and the weights sum to 1, with no cap on any one stock and no transaction costs.

criteria: Given any portfolio formed in the study, when its weights are read, then each is ≥ 0 and they sum to 1 within 1e-9.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance rule picks the weights with the lowest portfolio variance under the estimate.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with variances 1 and 4, when the rule runs, then the weights are 0.8 and 0.2.

nodes.title: The risk-parity rule picks the weights for which every stock contributes equally to the portfolio variance under the estimate.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with volatilities 10% and 20%, when the rule runs, then the weights are 2/3 and 1/3.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk-parity rule clusters the stocks into a tree by correlation, then splits the weight down the tree, giving each branch of a split a share inversely proportional to its variance.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with variances 1 and 4, when the rule runs, then the weights are 0.8 and 0.2.
Given 4 stocks in 2 pairs, each pair correlated at 0.9 and the pairs uncorrelated, with equal variances, when the rule runs, then each pair gets 0.5 of the weight.

nodes.title: An equal-weight portfolio of each month's stocks is formed at every rebalance date and shown next to every rule's ranking as the floor.

criteria: Given 400 eligible stocks on R, when the study runs, then the equal-weight portfolio gives each 1/400.

nodes.title: Between rebalance dates, weights drift with prices. A stock that stops trading during the month counts its return through its last trading day, that day included, and its weight is then held as cash at 0% for the rest of the month.

criteria: Given a stock with 5% of the portfolio whose last trading day is the 10th trading day of the holding month, when the month's returns are computed, then its return counts through day 10, and from day 11 its drifted weight earns 0%.

nodes.title: A portfolio's realized variance for a holding month is the variance of its daily returns within that month, annualized ×252.

criteria: Given 20 daily portfolio returns alternating +1% and −1%, when realized variance is computed, then it is 0.0001 × 252 = 0.0252.

nodes.title: For each rule, the four estimates are ranked by mean realized variance over all holding months, lowest first, with the equal-weight portfolio shown alongside.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the league table is read, then each of the 3 rules lists 4 estimates in increasing mean realized variance, plus the equal-weight value.

nodes.title: Turnover is half the sum of absolute weight changes from the drifted weights to the new weights at each rebalance date, averaged over all rebalance dates, and reported as a number for every estimate and rule without affecting the ranking.

criteria: Given drifted weights (0.6, 0.4) and new weights (0.5, 0.5), when turnover is computed, then it is 0.1.

nodes.title: For each rule, the winner is tested against the sample estimate with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, on the paired monthly realized variances: the null is that the winner's realized variance is no lower. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after correction across the 3 rules. The report states, for each rule, whether the null is rejected and the corrected p-value.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the significance part is read, then each of the 3 rules shows its winner, the corrected p-value and whether the null is rejected.
Given a rule whose winner is the sample estimate, when the significance part is read, then that rule says no test is needed.

nodes.title: The study report can be opened in the app.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the researcher opens it in the app, then its three parts' tables and charts are shown.

nodes.title: The full study runs in ≤ 1 hour.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine on the full history since 1998-01-02.

nodes.title: Each eligible member's target for R is the sum of its daily residual returns over the month after R: each day's return with the part explained by the components above the noise edge (at least 1) removed, the components and the stock's exposure to them being those fitted on the 252 trading days ending R (STRUC-04).

criteria: Given a synthetic stock whose residual daily returns in the month after R are +1.0%, −0.5% and +0.2%, when its target is computed, then it is +0.7%.
Given a synthetic one-factor window where the month after R follows the window's factor model with no noise, when targets are computed, then every target is 0 within 1e-9.
Given a stock whose last trading day is the 10th trading day of the month after R, when its target is computed, then it sums the residual returns through day 10, that day included.

nodes.title: Each eligible member has 13 base features for R, each computed from the 252 trading days ending R (prices adjusted as of R, RET-05):

Each of the 9 return-based features (both momentums, both reversals, both volatilities, maximum return, skewness, illiquidity) also has a residual version, computed the same way from the stock's residual daily returns in the window ending R (STRUC-04), with returns over a span summed rather than compounded, giving 22 candidate features in all.

criteria: Given a completed feature build, when the candidates for R are listed, then there are exactly 22: the 13 base features and 9 residual versions.
Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when the residual 1-month reversal is computed, then it equals the sum of the stock's residual returns over the last 21 days of the window.

nodes.title: The features are profiled with the data-analysis skill on every rebalance date: coverage (the share of eligible members with a value), distribution summaries and tails, and the rank correlation between every pair of candidates. It passes when the report has all three for every candidate across all rebalance dates.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the profile part of its report is read, then each of the 22 candidates has its coverage by rebalance date, its distribution summary and its correlations with the other 21.

nodes.title: Every feature for R, and the components and exposures its target uses, are built from no data after R; only the target's own month comes after R.

criteria: Given a price or volume changed on a day after R, when the study is run again, then every feature for R and earlier is identical.
Given a return changed on a day after the month that follows R, when the study is run again, then the target for R is identical.

nodes.title: One command runs the whole study and writes one report with five parts: feature profile, per-feature verdicts, combined models, controls and holdout record.

criteria: Given stored data from 1998-01-02, when the command is run, then one report is written that has all five parts.

nodes.title: Rebalance dates before 2021-09-30 are the development months; rebalance dates from 2021-09-30 onward are the holdout, the final ~5 years at the time of writing. The boundary is fixed and does not move as data is added.

criteria: Given data through 2026-09-30, when the study runs, then the holdout is the 60 rebalance dates from 2021-09-30 to 2026-08-31.
Given a later refresh that adds a year of data, when the study runs, then the first holdout date is still 2021-09-30.

nodes.title: A development run uses no data from after 2021-09-30.

criteria: Given a price, volume or return changed on a day after 2021-09-30, when the development run is repeated, then every result in its report is identical.

nodes.title: The holdout is scored only when the researcher asks for it, after freezing the settings; the report records the date it was scored and the frozen settings, and any later scoring of the holdout is labelled "holdout reused".

criteria: Given a development run, when its report is read, then no holdout result is shown and the holdout record says "not yet scored".
Given the holdout scored on day H, when the report is read, then it states H and every setting used.
Given the holdout already scored, when it is scored again with any settings, then the new report is labelled "holdout reused" and still states the first scoring date.

nodes.title: The combined models are trained walk-forward: the first test month is the 61st rebalance date, and the models are refit every 12 rebalance dates on all earlier rebalance dates whose target month has ended by the refit date. Model settings are chosen on development months only; holdout months are predicted with the frozen settings, refit on the same schedule.

criteria: Given a refit on rebalance date R, when its training months are listed, then every one is earlier than R and its target month ended on or before R.
Given the first test month, when its training months are counted, then there are 60.

nodes.title: A prediction's score is the mean, over test months, of the monthly rank correlation across stocks between the predictions and the targets; the out-of-sample R² is reported next to it.

criteria: Given a month where the predictions rank the stocks exactly as their targets, when scored, then that month's rank correlation is 1.
Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then every model and the baseline show both the score and the out-of-sample R².

nodes.title: Each candidate feature is tested on its own with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given the feature's monthly rank correlations with the targets: the null is that the feature carries no information, with its distribution from shuffling the feature across stocks within each month, two-sided. It passes on the development months only if the null is rejected at 5% after Holm correction across the 22 candidates, and on the holdout only if it is rejected again, with the same sign, at 5% after Holm correction across the features that passed on development months.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the per-feature part is read, then each of the 22 candidates shows its mean rank correlation, its corrected p-value and whether it passed, for the development months and, once scored, the holdout.

nodes.title: The baseline is the single candidate feature with the highest training rank correlation in absolute value, used with its sign as the prediction, chosen again at every refit.

criteria: Given a refit where 1-month reversal has the training rank correlation of largest magnitude, −0.04, when the baseline predicts, then its prediction is minus that feature.

nodes.title: Two combined models, one linear and one non-linear, each predict the targets from all 22 candidates.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then both models show their scores on the development test months and, once scored, the holdout.

nodes.title: Each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill against the same model retrained walk-forward on targets shuffled across stocks within each month: the null is that its score is no higher than under shuffled targets. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 2 models.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then each model shows its corrected p-value against shuffled targets and whether the null is rejected.

nodes.title: Each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill against the baseline (INFO-08), on the paired monthly rank correlations: the null is that the model's score is no higher than the baseline's. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 2 models.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then each model shows its corrected p-value against the baseline and whether the null is rejected.

nodes.title: Each feature's contribution to each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill: the feature is shuffled across stocks within each test month and the model's score recomputed, and the null is that the score does not fall. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 22 candidates within that model.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the per-feature part is read, then each candidate shows, for each model, its fall in score, its corrected p-value and whether it passed.

nodes.title: Each candidate gets one verdict, survives or not: it survives only if it passes INFO-07 on both the development months and the holdout. Until the holdout is scored, the verdict reads "development only".

criteria: Given a feature that passes INFO-07 on the development months but not on the holdout, when the verdict is read, then it does not survive.
Given a study where no feature survives, when the report is read, then it says so plainly, with every feature's figures still shown.

nodes.title: A planted feature is the required positive control: built from the targets plus independent noise so that its true rank correlation with them is 0.03, it is tested as in INFO-07, in the same Holm family, and must pass on the development months. It is never used by the combined models or the baseline.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the controls part is read, then the planted feature's rank correlation, corrected p-value and pass or fail are shown.

nodes.title: 100 pure-noise features, drawn independently of all data, are the required negative control: each is tested as in INFO-07 before correction, and between 1 and 10 of the 100 may be rejected at 5%. They are never used by the combined models or the baseline.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the controls part is read, then the number of noise features rejected out of 100 is shown with pass or fail.

nodes.title: If either required control fails, the report states at its top that the tests can't be trusted.

criteria: Given a study where the planted feature does not pass, when the report is opened, then its first line says the tests can't be trusted and names the failed control.

nodes.title: Whether 1-month reversal passes INFO-07 on real data is reported in the controls part as a known-effect check; its failing does not mark the tests untrustworthy.

criteria: Given a study where 1-month reversal does not pass, when the report is read, then the controls part says so and the report is not marked untrustworthy for it.

nodes.title: The feature study's report can be opened in the app.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the researcher opens it in the app, then its five parts' tables and charts are shown.

nodes.title: The full study, nulls included, runs in ≤ 4 hours.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine on the full history since 1998-01-02.

nodes.title: Daily data from 1998 onward (first trading day 1998-01-02) to the last completed trading day: unadjusted open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member on any day in that range, for every day it traded on a major US exchange.

criteria: Given any member on any date since 1998-01-02, when its prices are requested, then a close exists for every trading day it was listed on a major exchange.

nodes.title: Every split, cash dividend (regular and special), ticker change, merger, acquisition and delisting for those stocks since 1998, with its effective or ex-date.

criteria: Given any of the 10 names in DATA-04, when its corporate actions are requested, then its final event (acquisition, merger or delisting) is present.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership history since 1998 with the effective date of every addition and removal, including companies that later left or were delisted; no ETFs, over-the-counter stocks or preferred shares.

criteria: Given the stored membership, when every member on every date is listed, then none is an ETF, an over-the-counter listing or a preferred share.

nodes.title: The 10 named former S&P 500 members are present with 2 end dates each (20 in all), an index exit date and a last trading day on a major exchange, each one equal to this reference table:
Every stored value carries the date it was first known to the system, and every replaced value is kept with the date it was replaced.

criteria: Given a value revised by the source on day V, when data is requested as known on V − 1, then the earlier value is returned.

nodes.title: The universe and total returns for one date come back in ≤ 2 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine for 20 random dates since 1998; every one ≤ 2 s.

nodes.title: Full daily total-return series from 1998-01-02 to the latest loaded day for one date's ~500 members come back in ≤ 30 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine for 5 random dates; every one ≤ 30 s.

nodes.title: No data is bought beyond the existing primary-source subscription, and the independent source is used only within its free access.

criteria: Checked at architecture review: every data source used is the existing subscription or free.

nodes.title: The independent source is used only for spot-checks: no more than the CHECK-01 sample is fetched per validation run unless a full check is requested.

criteria: Given a standard validation run, when its fetch log is read, then at most 100 stocks were requested.

nodes.title: Data-source credentials are never shown in the app, in run logs or in run summaries.

criteria: Given a refresh with credentials configured, when its log, summary and the app are searched for the credential value, then it appears nowhere.

acceptance: Each M1 type is code in its owner's `types.py` (pandera for frames, Pydantic for the rest) with the store schema in `store/schema.py`; every `tests/contracts/eqdata.*/` and `tests/contracts/server.api_*/` sample, one per contract case, validates, the `PrimarySource` replay double derived from PB-01's and PB-02's samples

Every M1 step and entry imports with its contract signature, body `raise NotImplementedError("<its task>")`; each `__init__.py` exports its contract; `eqdata`'s `__main__.py` dispatches `refresh`, `returns` and `universe`, `eqdata_server`'s dispatches `eqdata-server`, and `web`'s shell routes to `InspectRoutes`; `packages/web/src/api/generated.ts` is generated from the stubbed app's `/openapi.json`

The `eqdata.validate` fake and the `search_companies`, `universe`, `universe_sizes`, `prices`, `timeline` and `source_diffs` fakes serve their `tests/contracts/eqdata.*/` fixtures; a mock server serves the `server.api_*` samples for `web`; the golden-case store builder loads a fixture's `input.json` into a temporary store; shared test fixtures live in `tests/support/`, never the protected `tests/conftest.py` (UR-53)

`start_run` inserts a `runs` row with the PID; `finish_run` writes the summary and releases the lock; `fail_run` marks the run `failed`; each output validates against its contract sample; signatures unchanged
`StoreProgress(run)` appends each call as a numbered `RunEvent`; its event stream matches the `eqdata.StoreProgress` replay double for a 3-step refresh with one warning; signature unchanged

`SyntheticPrimarySource(seed=0)` satisfies `eqdata.PrimarySource` with 5 companies over 2 years holding one split, one dividend, one delisting and one reused ticker, in PB-01's raw table shape; `with_changes(duplicates=2, revised_closes=1, seed=17)` plants TC-17's incremental; same seed, same rows
`download` on the `PrimarySource` replay double and an empty `RefreshMark` returns `RawTables` that validate against their sample, one progress call per table; signature unchanged

`clean` keeps the last of each duplicate (company, date) row, counts the drops and keys rows by `permaticker`; both `eqdata.CleanTables` samples come out of their `RawTables` inputs; signature unchanged

`stage` clears old staging, writes the `CleanTables` samples to staging and returns a `StagedBatch` matching its replay double; the negative-close case is refused with the contract's error; signature unchanged

`commit` closes changed rows with `replaced_on` and inserts new ones with `known_from` in one transaction; the first-load and revised-close cases give their `eqdata.CommitResult` samples; signature unchanged

Every `eqdata.previous_trading_day` and `eqdata.trading_days` contract case passes from `exchange_calendars` XNYS sessions (Saturday → Friday, 2001-09-11 → 2001-09-10, Good Friday, January 1998 = 20 sessions, a weekend = empty); signatures unchanged

TC-08 passes: a reused ticker and a ticker change resolve by date to the right `company_id`

Given a company delisted before today, when `universe` is asked for a date it was a member, then it is listed; given an `identity_overrides.csv` split row, then the two companies get separate ids from the split date

nodes.title: For any past date, get the stocks that were investable on that date and their total returns, using only what was known then.
Know where the data might be wrong: every disagreement with an independent source is flagged, then explained or accepted.
See the data and its quality issues visually, without writing code.
Total returns as of a date
For a given date, the system returns every stock that was an S&P 500 member during that date, by the date each index change took effect.

criteria: Given an index addition announced on day A and effective on day E > A, when the universe is requested for any day from A to E − 1, then the stock is not in it; when requested for day E, then it is.
Given an index removal effective on day R, when the universe is requested for day R − 1, then the stock is in it; for day R, then it is not.

nodes.title: The universe for a date includes members that later left the index or stopped trading.

criteria: Given 2008-06-02, when the universe is requested, then Lehman Brothers, Bear Stearns, Countrywide, Merrill Lynch, Wachovia and Anheuser-Busch are all in it.

nodes.title: Each stock has a permanent identifier for the company, which is unchanged across ticker changes.

criteria: Given a company that changed ticker, when its membership is requested for dates before and after the change, then both carry the same identifier.

nodes.title: Each returned member carries the ticker it traded under on the requested date.

criteria: Given 2005-06-01, when the universe is requested, then the entry for Anheuser-Busch shows ticker BUD and the company is Anheuser-Busch, not today's holder of that ticker.

nodes.title: The system returns the number of members for every trading day in a date range.

criteria: Given 1998-01-02 to the latest loaded day, when universe sizes are requested, then every trading day has a count, and each count equals the length of that day's universe list.

nodes.title: For every stock that was investable on any date since 1998, the system returns its daily total-return series between two given dates.

criteria: Given any date D since 1998-01-02 and the universe for D, when total returns from D to D + 20 trading days are requested, then a series is returned for every member, including members that stopped trading in that window.

nodes.title: A daily total return combines the price change and any cash dividend going ex on that day.

criteria: Given a stock with a $0.50 dividend going ex on day T, a close of $50.00 on T − 1 and a close of $49.75 on T, when returns are requested, then the return for T is (49.75 + 0.50) / 50.00 − 1 = +0.50%.

nodes.title: Daily total returns are unaffected by stock splits.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split effective on day T with closes of $100.00 on T − 1 and $50.50 on T, when returns are requested, then the return for T is +1.00%.

nodes.title: Results requested as of date D use no information published after D.

criteria: Given a split or dividend that goes ex after D, when returns or prices are requested as of D, then the values up to D are identical to those produced before that event was loaded.

nodes.title: Price levels are available unadjusted, or adjusted only for splits and dividends that went ex on or before the as-of date.

criteria: Given a 2-for-1 split on day S > D, when adjusted prices are requested as of D, then they equal the unadjusted prices for every day up to D.

nodes.title: A stock's return series runs through its last trading day, including the return on that last day.

criteria: Given Lehman Brothers, when returns through 2008-09-30 are requested, then the return for 2008-09-15 is present and below −90%.
Given a company acquired for cash, when returns are requested, then the return on its last trading day is present and the series ends that day.

nodes.title: Every returned series states whether each day is a trading day with a price, or a gap.

criteria: Given a trading halt with no close on day T, when returns are requested, then day T is marked as a gap and has no invented return.

nodes.title: A refresh downloads data from the primary source.

criteria: Given an empty store, when a refresh is started, then afterwards prices, corporate actions, company identities and index membership are stored for every S&P 500 member from 1998-01-02 to the last completed trading day.

nodes.title: A refresh fetches only data newer than what is already stored.

criteria: Given data stored through day T, when a refresh is started on day T + 1 after the close, then only day T + 1 and any corrections the source issued since the last refresh are downloaded.

nodes.title: A refresh cleans the data before it is stored.

criteria: Given a downloaded row with a duplicate (stock, date), when the refresh runs, then one row is stored and the duplicate is reported in the run summary.

nodes.title: A refresh ends with a validation run (CHECK-01), and its results go to the run summary.

criteria: Given a completed refresh, when its summary is viewed, then it lists the number of rows added, rows changed, and new findings.

nodes.title: A refresh that fails leaves the stored data as it was before the refresh started.

criteria: Given a refresh interrupted after half its downloads, when the universe or returns are requested, then the results are identical to those before the refresh.

nodes.title: A refresh started while another is running is refused.

criteria: Given a refresh in progress, when a second is started, then it is refused with a message naming the running one.

nodes.title: Each run of a refresh or validation is started on demand, from the command line or from the app.

criteria: Given the app open, when the researcher starts a refresh there, then it runs exactly as one started from the command line.

nodes.title: A validation run checks 100 members that the independent source still carries, sampled across 1998 to today.

criteria: Given a validation run, when it finishes, then it has compared exactly 100 stocks (or all available, if fewer), and every calendar year from 1998 to today has at least 2 stocks that were members in that year.

nodes.title: For each sampled stock, the run also checks every split and special dividend that stock had.

criteria: Given a sampled stock with 3 splits and 1 special dividend since 1998, when the run finishes, then all 4 events have been compared.

nodes.title: A full validation run, on demand, checks every member the independent source carries.

criteria: Given a full validation run, when it finishes, then every member the independent source carries has been compared.

nodes.title: Splits agree only when the date and the ratio match exactly.

criteria: Given a 3-for-2 split on one source and a 2-for-1 split on the same date on the other, when compared, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Dividends agree only when the ex-date matches and the amount is within $0.001.

criteria: Given amounts of $0.2500 and $0.2509 on the same ex-date, when compared, then they agree; given $0.2500 and $0.2515, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Daily total returns agree when they are within 5 basis points (0.05 percentage points) of each other.

criteria: Given returns of +1.20% and +1.24% for the same stock and day, when compared, then they agree; given +1.20% and +1.26%, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: Unadjusted closes agree when they are within 0.5% of each other.

criteria: Given closes of $40.00 and $40.18, when compared, then they agree; given $40.00 and $40.25, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: A stock the independent source doesn't carry is checked for missing trading days before its last trading day.

criteria: Given a delisted stock with no price on a day when the exchange was open and the stock was not halted, when checked, then a finding is raised for that day.

nodes.title: A stock acquired for a known cash price is checked for a last close consistent with the deal.

criteria: Given a cash acquisition at $70.00 a share and a last close of $69.95, when checked, then it passes; given a last close more than 2% from the deal price, then a finding is raised.

nodes.title: A stock's index membership is checked to end no later than its last trading day.

nodes.title: Findings from internal checks are listed and resolved in the same way as disagreements with the independent source.

criteria: Given a CHECK-08 finding and a CHECK-06 finding, when findings are listed, then both appear in one list with the same fields and the same resolve actions.

nodes.title: Each finding records the stock, the date(s), the check that raised it, both values, and the difference.

criteria: Given any finding, when viewed, then all five are shown.

nodes.title: A resolved finding stays resolved in later runs while both values are unchanged.

criteria: Given an explained finding, when the next run finds the same difference, then no new finding is raised; when either value has changed, then the finding is reopened.

nodes.title: The 10 named former members are present with both end dates matching the reference table in DATA-04.

criteria: Given each of the 10 names, when checked, then its index exit date and its last trading day on a major exchange each equal the table's value, or a finding is raised for each one that differs.

nodes.title: The exploratory analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on the full stored history. It covers summary statistics and tails of daily total returns by year, missing days per stock, universe size over time, and the number of corporate actions per year.

criteria: Given a completed refresh, when the analysis runs, then its report has a section for each of the four, covering every year from 1998 to today.

nodes.title: Each anomaly the analysis identifies becomes a finding.

criteria: Given a stock with a daily return above +100% and no corporate action on that day, when the analysis runs, then a finding is raised for that stock and day.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock, the app shows its unadjusted and adjusted price history.

criteria: Given Eastman Kodak, when chosen, then both price series are shown for 1998 to its last trading day.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock, the app shows a timeline of its corporate actions, ticker changes and index entry and exit.

criteria: Given Wachovia, when chosen, then its index exit and last trading day appear on the timeline.

nodes.title: For a chosen stock that was compared, the app shows its daily differences from the independent source over time, with the agreement thresholds marked.

criteria: Given a sampled stock, when chosen, then each day beyond a CHECK-06 or CHECK-07 threshold is highlighted.

nodes.title: The app shows S&P 500 member count per trading day from 1998 to the latest loaded day.

criteria: Given the chart, when the researcher points at a day, then that day's count and date are shown.

nodes.title: The app lists findings, filterable by status, check and stock.

criteria: Given 50 findings of which 10 are open, when filtered to open, then exactly 10 are shown.

nodes.title: The researcher can resolve a finding from the app.

criteria: Given an open finding, when marked explained with a reason in the app, then its status changes as in CHECK-13.

nodes.title: For a chosen date, the app shows that date's universe.

criteria: Given 2008-06-02, when chosen, then the list shows every member with its ticker on that date.

nodes.title: The app shows data views, quality tools and the reports that commands write; it has no screening or interactive research views.

criteria: Given the app, when every page is opened, then none ranks or filters stocks by return or signal.

nodes.title: The app shows a running refresh's or validation's current step and percentage complete, updated as the run advances.

criteria: Given a running refresh, when the app is open, then the shown step and percentage change within 2 seconds of the run advancing, without reloading the page.

nodes.title: Errors and warnings appear in the app as they happen during a run.

criteria: Given a stock the independent source rejects, when it happens, then a warning naming the stock appears within 2 seconds.

nodes.title: A run started from the command line also shows its progress in the app.

criteria: Given a refresh started from the command line, when the app is opened, then the run is shown with its current progress.

nodes.title: Finished runs are listed with start time, end time, outcome and summary.

criteria: Given 3 finished runs, when the run list is opened, then all 3 are shown, newest first.

nodes.title: The structure analysis is run with the data-analysis skill on every rebalance date's window: the eligible members of PORT-03 over the 252 trading days ending that day. It passes when the report has, for every window, the eigenvalue spectrum, the market factor's share of variance, and the raw and residual mean absolute correlation.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the structure part of its report is read, then each of the three is present for every rebalance date.

nodes.title: For each window, the eigenvalues of the members' correlation matrix are compared with the random-matrix (Marchenko–Pastur) noise edge for that window's number of days and stocks, and the number of eigenvalues above the edge is reported.

criteria: Given a synthetic window of 252 days and 400 stocks with independent returns, when analysed, then at most 1 eigenvalue is above the edge.
Given a synthetic window of 252 days and 400 stocks driven by one common factor that explains 40% of each stock's variance, when analysed, then exactly 1 eigenvalue is above the edge.

nodes.title: For each window, the market factor's share of variance is the largest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix divided by the number of stocks, reported as a series over time.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when analysed, then the share is 0.40 ± 0.03.

nodes.title: For each window, the principal components above the noise edge (at least 1) are removed from every stock's returns, and the mean absolute pairwise correlation of what remains is reported next to the raw value, with the number of components removed.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when analysed, then 1 component is removed, the raw mean absolute correlation is ≥ 0.35, and the residual one is ≤ 0.08.

nodes.title: Each window's results use only the returns inside that window.

criteria: Given a return changed on a day after rebalance date R, when the study is run again, then every structure result for R and earlier windows is identical.

nodes.title: One command runs the whole study and writes one report with three parts: structure, league table and significance.

criteria: Given stored data from 1998-01-02, when the command is run, then one report is written that has all three parts.

nodes.title: Rebalance dates are the last trading day of each month, from the first month-end on which 252 trading days have passed since 1998-01-02 to the last month-end whose following month is complete.

criteria: Given data from 1998-01-02 to 2026-09-30, when the study runs, then every rebalance date is a month's last trading day, the first is the first month-end with 252 trading days behind it, and the last is 2026-08-31.

nodes.title: At each rebalance date, the portfolios hold that day's members (UNIV-01) that have 252 trading days of returns ending that day; members with fewer are left out that month, and the number left out is reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given a stock added to the index with 100 trading days of history on rebalance date R, when the study runs, then the stock is in no portfolio formed on R, and R's left-out count includes it.

nodes.title: Every estimate and every weight formed on rebalance date R uses no return from after R.

criteria: Given a return changed on a day after R, when the study is run again, then every estimate and weight formed on R or earlier is identical.

nodes.title: The sample estimate is the sample covariance of the window's daily returns.

criteria: Given a synthetic window, when estimated, then it equals the sample covariance of those returns.

nodes.title: The shrinkage estimate pulls the sample covariance toward a constant-correlation target (each stock's own sample variance, and one correlation shared by every pair equal to the window's average sample correlation), by an intensity estimated from the window and reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given any window, when estimated, then the result equals (1 − δ) × sample + δ × target with 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1, and δ is reported.

nodes.title: The denoised estimate replaces the correlation matrix's eigenvalues below the noise edge of STRUC-02 with their average, keeps those above it, and rescales to each stock's sample variance.

criteria: Given any window, when estimated, then the eigenvalues above the edge are unchanged, those below it are all equal, the matrix's trace is unchanged, and its diagonal equals the sample variances.

nodes.title: The factor-model estimate is built from the principal components above the noise edge (at least 1) plus each stock's own residual variance, and the number of components is reported for every rebalance date.

criteria: Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when estimated, then 1 component is used and the diagonal equals the sample variances.

nodes.title: Every portfolio is long-only and fully invested: no weight is negative and the weights sum to 1, with no cap on any one stock and no transaction costs.

criteria: Given any portfolio formed in the study, when its weights are read, then each is ≥ 0 and they sum to 1 within 1e-9.

nodes.title: The minimum-variance rule picks the weights with the lowest portfolio variance under the estimate.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with variances 1 and 4, when the rule runs, then the weights are 0.8 and 0.2.

nodes.title: The risk-parity rule picks the weights for which every stock contributes equally to the portfolio variance under the estimate.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with volatilities 10% and 20%, when the rule runs, then the weights are 2/3 and 1/3.

nodes.title: The hierarchical risk-parity rule clusters the stocks into a tree by correlation, then splits the weight down the tree, giving each branch of a split a share inversely proportional to its variance.

criteria: Given 2 uncorrelated stocks with variances 1 and 4, when the rule runs, then the weights are 0.8 and 0.2.
Given 4 stocks in 2 pairs, each pair correlated at 0.9 and the pairs uncorrelated, with equal variances, when the rule runs, then each pair gets 0.5 of the weight.

nodes.title: An equal-weight portfolio of each month's stocks is formed at every rebalance date and shown next to every rule's ranking as the floor.

criteria: Given 400 eligible stocks on R, when the study runs, then the equal-weight portfolio gives each 1/400.

nodes.title: Between rebalance dates, weights drift with prices. A stock that stops trading during the month counts its return through its last trading day, that day included, and its weight is then held as cash at 0% for the rest of the month.

criteria: Given a stock with 5% of the portfolio whose last trading day is the 10th trading day of the holding month, when the month's returns are computed, then its return counts through day 10, and from day 11 its drifted weight earns 0%.

nodes.title: A portfolio's realized variance for a holding month is the variance of its daily returns within that month, annualized ×252.

criteria: Given 20 daily portfolio returns alternating +1% and −1%, when realized variance is computed, then it is 0.0001 × 252 = 0.0252.

nodes.title: For each rule, the four estimates are ranked by mean realized variance over all holding months, lowest first, with the equal-weight portfolio shown alongside.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the league table is read, then each of the 3 rules lists 4 estimates in increasing mean realized variance, plus the equal-weight value.

nodes.title: Turnover is half the sum of absolute weight changes from the drifted weights to the new weights at each rebalance date, averaged over all rebalance dates, and reported as a number for every estimate and rule without affecting the ranking.

criteria: Given drifted weights (0.6, 0.4) and new weights (0.5, 0.5), when turnover is computed, then it is 0.1.

nodes.title: For each rule, the winner is tested against the sample estimate with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, on the paired monthly realized variances: the null is that the winner's realized variance is no lower. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after correction across the 3 rules. The report states, for each rule, whether the null is rejected and the corrected p-value.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the significance part is read, then each of the 3 rules shows its winner, the corrected p-value and whether the null is rejected.
Given a rule whose winner is the sample estimate, when the significance part is read, then that rule says no test is needed.

nodes.title: The study report can be opened in the app.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the researcher opens it in the app, then its three parts' tables and charts are shown.

nodes.title: The full study runs in ≤ 1 hour.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine on the full history since 1998-01-02.

nodes.title: Each eligible member's target for R is the sum of its daily residual returns over the month after R: each day's return with the part explained by the components above the noise edge (at least 1) removed, the components and the stock's exposure to them being those fitted on the 252 trading days ending R (STRUC-04).

criteria: Given a synthetic stock whose residual daily returns in the month after R are +1.0%, −0.5% and +0.2%, when its target is computed, then it is +0.7%.
Given a synthetic one-factor window where the month after R follows the window's factor model with no noise, when targets are computed, then every target is 0 within 1e-9.
Given a stock whose last trading day is the 10th trading day of the month after R, when its target is computed, then it sums the residual returns through day 10, that day included.

nodes.title: Each eligible member has 13 base features for R, each computed from the 252 trading days ending R (prices adjusted as of R, RET-05):

Each of the 9 return-based features (both momentums, both reversals, both volatilities, maximum return, skewness, illiquidity) also has a residual version, computed the same way from the stock's residual daily returns in the window ending R (STRUC-04), with returns over a span summed rather than compounded, giving 22 candidate features in all.

criteria: Given a completed feature build, when the candidates for R are listed, then there are exactly 22: the 13 base features and 9 residual versions.
Given the one-factor synthetic window of STRUC-02, when the residual 1-month reversal is computed, then it equals the sum of the stock's residual returns over the last 21 days of the window.

nodes.title: The features are profiled with the data-analysis skill on every rebalance date: coverage (the share of eligible members with a value), distribution summaries and tails, and the rank correlation between every pair of candidates. It passes when the report has all three for every candidate across all rebalance dates.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the profile part of its report is read, then each of the 22 candidates has its coverage by rebalance date, its distribution summary and its correlations with the other 21.

nodes.title: Every feature for R, and the components and exposures its target uses, are built from no data after R; only the target's own month comes after R.

criteria: Given a price or volume changed on a day after R, when the study is run again, then every feature for R and earlier is identical.
Given a return changed on a day after the month that follows R, when the study is run again, then the target for R is identical.

nodes.title: One command runs the whole study and writes one report with five parts: feature profile, per-feature verdicts, combined models, controls and holdout record.

criteria: Given stored data from 1998-01-02, when the command is run, then one report is written that has all five parts.

nodes.title: Rebalance dates before 2021-09-30 are the development months; rebalance dates from 2021-09-30 onward are the holdout, the final ~5 years at the time of writing. The boundary is fixed and does not move as data is added.

criteria: Given data through 2026-09-30, when the study runs, then the holdout is the 60 rebalance dates from 2021-09-30 to 2026-08-31.
Given a later refresh that adds a year of data, when the study runs, then the first holdout date is still 2021-09-30.

nodes.title: A development run uses no data from after 2021-09-30.

criteria: Given a price, volume or return changed on a day after 2021-09-30, when the development run is repeated, then every result in its report is identical.

nodes.title: The holdout is scored only when the researcher asks for it, after freezing the settings; the report records the date it was scored and the frozen settings, and any later scoring of the holdout is labelled "holdout reused".

criteria: Given a development run, when its report is read, then no holdout result is shown and the holdout record says "not yet scored".
Given the holdout scored on day H, when the report is read, then it states H and every setting used.
Given the holdout already scored, when it is scored again with any settings, then the new report is labelled "holdout reused" and still states the first scoring date.

nodes.title: The combined models are trained walk-forward: the first test month is the 61st rebalance date, and the models are refit every 12 rebalance dates on all earlier rebalance dates whose target month has ended by the refit date. Model settings are chosen on development months only; holdout months are predicted with the frozen settings, refit on the same schedule.

criteria: Given a refit on rebalance date R, when its training months are listed, then every one is earlier than R and its target month ended on or before R.
Given the first test month, when its training months are counted, then there are 60.

nodes.title: A prediction's score is the mean, over test months, of the monthly rank correlation across stocks between the predictions and the targets; the out-of-sample R² is reported next to it.

criteria: Given a month where the predictions rank the stocks exactly as their targets, when scored, then that month's rank correlation is 1.
Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then every model and the baseline show both the score and the out-of-sample R².

nodes.title: Each candidate feature is tested on its own with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given the feature's monthly rank correlations with the targets: the null is that the feature carries no information, with its distribution from shuffling the feature across stocks within each month, two-sided. It passes on the development months only if the null is rejected at 5% after Holm correction across the 22 candidates, and on the holdout only if it is rejected again, with the same sign, at 5% after Holm correction across the features that passed on development months.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the per-feature part is read, then each of the 22 candidates shows its mean rank correlation, its corrected p-value and whether it passed, for the development months and, once scored, the holdout.

nodes.title: The baseline is the single candidate feature with the highest training rank correlation in absolute value, used with its sign as the prediction, chosen again at every refit.

criteria: Given a refit where 1-month reversal has the training rank correlation of largest magnitude, −0.04, when the baseline predicts, then its prediction is minus that feature.

nodes.title: Two combined models, one linear and one non-linear, each predict the targets from all 22 candidates.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then both models show their scores on the development test months and, once scored, the holdout.

nodes.title: Each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill against the same model retrained walk-forward on targets shuffled across stocks within each month: the null is that its score is no higher than under shuffled targets. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 2 models.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then each model shows its corrected p-value against shuffled targets and whether the null is rejected.

nodes.title: Each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill against the baseline (INFO-08), on the paired monthly rank correlations: the null is that the model's score is no higher than the baseline's. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 2 models.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the combined-models part is read, then each model shows its corrected p-value against the baseline and whether the null is rejected.

nodes.title: Each feature's contribution to each combined model is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill: the feature is shuffled across stocks within each test month and the model's score recomputed, and the null is that the score does not fall. It passes only if the null is rejected one-sided at 5% after Holm correction across the 22 candidates within that model.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the per-feature part is read, then each candidate shows, for each model, its fall in score, its corrected p-value and whether it passed.

nodes.title: Each candidate gets one verdict, survives or not: it survives only if it passes INFO-07 on both the development months and the holdout. Until the holdout is scored, the verdict reads "development only".

criteria: Given a feature that passes INFO-07 on the development months but not on the holdout, when the verdict is read, then it does not survive.
Given a study where no feature survives, when the report is read, then it says so plainly, with every feature's figures still shown.

nodes.title: A planted feature is the required positive control: built from the targets plus independent noise so that its true rank correlation with them is 0.03, it is tested as in INFO-07, in the same Holm family, and must pass on the development months. It is never used by the combined models or the baseline.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the controls part is read, then the planted feature's rank correlation, corrected p-value and pass or fail are shown.

nodes.title: 100 pure-noise features, drawn independently of all data, are the required negative control: each is tested as in INFO-07 before correction, and between 1 and 10 of the 100 may be rejected at 5%. They are never used by the combined models or the baseline.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the controls part is read, then the number of noise features rejected out of 100 is shown with pass or fail.

nodes.title: If either required control fails, the report states at its top that the tests can't be trusted.

criteria: Given a study where the planted feature does not pass, when the report is opened, then its first line says the tests can't be trusted and names the failed control.

nodes.title: Whether 1-month reversal passes INFO-07 on real data is reported in the controls part as a known-effect check; its failing does not mark the tests untrustworthy.

criteria: Given a study where 1-month reversal does not pass, when the report is read, then the controls part says so and the report is not marked untrustworthy for it.

nodes.title: The feature study's report can be opened in the app.

criteria: Given a completed study, when the researcher opens it in the app, then its five parts' tables and charts are shown.

nodes.title: The full study, nulls included, runs in ≤ 4 hours.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine on the full history since 1998-01-02.

nodes.title: Daily data from 1998 onward (first trading day 1998-01-02) to the last completed trading day: unadjusted open, high, low, close and volume for every stock that was an S&P 500 member on any day in that range, for every day it traded on a major US exchange.

criteria: Given any member on any date since 1998-01-02, when its prices are requested, then a close exists for every trading day it was listed on a major exchange.

nodes.title: Every split, cash dividend (regular and special), ticker change, merger, acquisition and delisting for those stocks since 1998, with its effective or ex-date.

criteria: Given any of the 10 names in DATA-04, when its corporate actions are requested, then its final event (acquisition, merger or delisting) is present.

nodes.title: S&P 500 membership history since 1998 with the effective date of every addition and removal, including companies that later left or were delisted; no ETFs, over-the-counter stocks or preferred shares.

criteria: Given the stored membership, when every member on every date is listed, then none is an ETF, an over-the-counter listing or a preferred share.

nodes.title: The 10 named former S&P 500 members are present with 2 end dates each (20 in all), an index exit date and a last trading day on a major exchange, each one equal to this reference table:
Every stored value carries the date it was first known to the system, and every replaced value is kept with the date it was replaced.

criteria: Given a value revised by the source on day V, when data is requested as known on V − 1, then the earlier value is returned.

nodes.title: The universe and total returns for one date come back in ≤ 2 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine for 20 random dates since 1998; every one ≤ 2 s.

nodes.title: Full daily total-return series from 1998-01-02 to the latest loaded day for one date's ~500 members come back in ≤ 30 seconds.

criteria: Timed on the researcher's machine for 5 random dates; every one ≤ 30 s.

nodes.title: No data is bought beyond the existing primary-source subscription, and the independent source is used only within its free access.

criteria: Checked at architecture review: every data source used is the existing subscription or free.

nodes.title: The independent source is used only for spot-checks: no more than the CHECK-01 sample is fetched per validation run unless a full check is requested.

criteria: Given a standard validation run, when its fetch log is read, then at most 100 stocks were requested.

nodes.title: Data-source credentials are never shown in the app, in run logs or in run summaries.

criteria: Given a refresh with credentials configured, when its log, summary and the app are searched for the credential value, then it appears nowhere.
